title: Jude and the Asset
premise: Xanthe Nakamura, a freelance hostage negotiator who works the cases agencies won't attach their names to, answers a burner phone and hears the voice of Daniel Reyes—the hostage she failed to save three years ago, alive and calling from inside Meridian, the deniable training program that manufactured negotiators like her. The call is bait: Meridian's handlers have marked Xanthe as an 'asset requiring retrieval,' and Daniel, presumed dead, is their leverage. As she traces the network that trained her, she discovers her one failure was engineered to test her loyalty, and that staying invisible means letting Daniel die for real. In the end, Xanthe burns Meridian's command structure by turning their own negotiation protocols against them, trading her anonymity—and the last of her old life—to walk Daniel out alive.
about_author: Astrid Marchetti is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to people talk themselves back from the edge before turning those voices into fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose professional calm hides private wreckage, and she lives in Lisbon with an unreliable cat.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Between jobs in a rented apartment in Rotterdam, Xanthe takes a call on a burner reserved for dead clients' families—only to hear Daniel Reyes, the man whose death ended her agency career. He says four words—'they kept me breathing'—before the line dies. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in hope; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Failure on the Board
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe, with a flashback chapter to the Reyes negotiation three years prior. We see how she followed protocol perfectly and still lost him, how the debrief felt staged, and how she was quietly cut loose afterward. Present-day Xanthe realizes the timeline of her dismissal doesn't add up. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Following a payment trail only a negotiator would know to read, she finds Meridian—a shell consultancy that trains deniable intermediaries for kidnappings states won't touch. She recognizes the curriculum because she lived it. A current trainee slips her a floor plan. Emotional beat: the horror of recognizing your own making.

chapters.title: Asset Retrieval
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe and a Meridian handler known only as Corvus. Corvus reports that Xanthe has tripped two tripwires; the order comes down to retrieve or retire her. Xanthe survives a staged mugging meant to test her reflexes and understands they're watching. Emotional beat: hunted, and realizing invisibility was always borrowed time.

chapters.title: The Voice Test
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Daniel calls again, and Xanthe—trained to detect coercion—catches the scripted cadence under his words: he's reading from a handler's sheet. But beneath it, a genuine plea: coordinates hidden in a misquoted Bible verse only he would choose. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—she can't tell if she's rescuing him or walking into the exercise.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe, joined briefly by her old mentor Ilsa Brandt, who once ran Meridian's intake. Ilsa confirms the program exists and reveals Xanthe's failure was designed—a loyalty test she passed by breaking down convincingly. Ilsa refuses to help further and warns her to run. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: What the Handlers Fear
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Instead of running, Xanthe goes on offense, using negotiation tradecraft to flip a mid-level Meridian accountant who hands over the rotation schedule and the location of the 'retirement facility.' She learns Daniel is scheduled for permanent retirement in nine days. Emotional beat: cold clarity; survival now means burning the network.

chapters.title: Corvus Opens the Line
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe and Corvus. Corvus calls to negotiate directly: Daniel's life for Xanthe's surrender. It's the first negotiation where she's both party and subject, and she plays it slow, extracting confirmations, buying hours, planting false intel through the accountant. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—herself as currency.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. At a decommissioned ferry terminal, the trade goes wrong exactly as she predicted: Meridian intends to take both. Using the protocols they taught her—silence, leverage, the concession that costs nothing—she turns Corvus's own team lead against him when his orders contradict the accountant's leaked documents. Gunfire, then quiet. Emotional beat: climax; every skill weaponized against its maker.

chapters.title: No Attribution
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe, closing with Daniel. Xanthe delivers the evidence to three journalists across three countries and lets Meridian eat itself in internal purges. She and Daniel part at a train platform—alive, unattributed, unbelonging. She keeps the burner. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; survival purchased with the self she used to be, and a fragile new loyalty worth the price.
